summary: Backend regression (iter 222) for the OT-flow simplification. Wrote 9 pytest cases in /app/backend/tests/test_ot_deprecation_iter222.py — all 9 PASSED. Verified: (1) POST /overtime/requests → 410 with deprecation detail. (2) PUT /overtime/requests/{id} → 410 (even with fake id). (3) GET /overtime/requests still returns 200 with seeded legacy row. (4) POST /overtime/requests/{id}/approve still works on directly-seeded pending legacy OTs. (5) DELETE /overtime/requests/{id} still works. (6) POST /overtime/periods with worked_entries (time_in/time_out on Sunday) auto-computes daily_entries=hours_holiday=8, estimated_amount=50000/192*8*2.0≈4166.67 (biweekly bug from iter221 stays fixed, not doubled). (7) /payroll/projection includes pending periodic OT. (8) POST /payroll/periods links BOTH linked_overtime_period_ids (periodic) AND linked_overtime_ids (legacy seeded approved OT) and marks both status=processed. (9) DELETE /payroll/periods releases BOTH collections back to status=approved with payroll_period_id cleared. Legacy OTs were seeded directly into MongoDB (since POST is now 410) using company_id/employee_id from an active employee.

critical_code_review_comments: people_ops.py is 7516 lines — still hugely over the 700-line guideline. Splitting into overtime.py / payroll.py / schedules.py modules remains the top structural debt item (called out in iter220 and iter221 as well).

The 410 endpoints return HTTPException(410, detail=...) which serializes as {"detail": "..."}. If any UI is showing a generic message, consider a machine-readable code (e.g. {"error_code": "OT_LEGACY_DEPRECATED"}) so the frontend can localize; not a blocker.

POST /overtime/periods response omits daily_entries (only totals). This forces the UI to do a GET-by-id after create to render the computed grid. Consider returning the persisted document (including daily_entries and worked_entries) directly to avoid the extra round-trip.

_create_overtime_request_legacy / _update_overtime_request_legacy internal helpers are still defined (unreachable from any route). Recommend either removing entirely once migrations are done or gating behind a super-admin-only route to reduce dead code.
seed_data_creation: Ephemeral: (a) temporarily set the first active employee's base_salary=50000 and payment_frequency=biweekly for deterministic math; restored on teardown. (b) 2 legacy overtime_requests seeded directly into MongoDB (POST is 410 now) with overtime_id prefix ot_TEST_iter222_*, wiped on teardown. (c) 1 periodic overtime_period_request via API (2026-05-10 Sunday shift) and 1 payroll period (biweekly 2026-05-01..15) — both cleaned by the test flow.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_ot_deprecation_iter222.py is idempotent (May 2026 dates + TEST_iter222 prefix + Mongo cleanup). Because POST /overtime/requests now returns 410, any future test needing a legacy OT MUST seed it directly to db.overtime_requests (or via /overtime/periods for the new path). The iter220 file test_payroll_ot_periodic_integration.py contains a class TestLegacyOTRegression that still calls POST /overtime/requests — that class will start FAILING on any future run because the endpoint is 410; leaving as-is per instructions (not modifying non-target tests). Consider that file for update in next iteration.
rca of the issue: N/A — this iteration was a positive-verification pass, not a bug-fix run. The simplification landed cleanly: deprecated writes return 410 with a clear detail message, and the entire payroll pipeline (projection, pending-in-range, period creation with linking, deletion with release) continues to consume BOTH overtime_period_requests (new) AND overtime_requests (legacy) so historical data is not orphaned.
